## Natural history notes

A tiny damselfly characterized by its extremely slender body, delicate clear wings, and pale green to bluish coloration with darker markings along the abdomen. In Florida, it is associated with wet prairies, marshes, sloughs, and other shallow freshwater wetlands with dense emergent grasses, sedges, and aquatic vegetation, especially in the Everglades region. Adults perch low and quietly among fine vegetation while hunting tiny flying insects, and the aquatic nymphs live among submerged plants where they feed on small aquatic invertebrates.
